title: Tenali Raman Tale 95 (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: While walking through an ancient cemetery outside Vijayanagara, King Krishnadevaraya kicked an old human skull that lay in the dry grass.... [KN]
full_text:
While walking through an ancient cemetery outside Vijayanagara, King Krishnadevaraya kicked an old human skull that lay in the dry grass.
The King sighed:
'Tenali, look upon this skull. It once had eyes that saw, ears that heard, and a tongue that spoke.
I wonder what fatal error brought this man to his early grave?'

Tenali bent down, examined the skull closely, and said with a solemn whisper:
'Maharaj, the skull just whispered its secret to me!'
The King stared: 'What did it say?'
Tenali replied:
'The skull whispered: "My tongue was too long, and my ears were too short; loose speech brought me to this dust!"'

The King scoffed: 'Nonsense! Skulls do not talk!'
Tenali insisted: 'I swear it, Maharaj! Bring the skull to court tomorrow, and it will speak before your throne!'

The next morning, the skull was placed upon a velvet cushion in the royal diwan.
The King commanded: 'Tenali, make the skull speak, or thou shalt be punished for mocking the Emperor!'

Tenali tapped the skull gently with his stylus:
'Speak, skull! Tell the Emperor how thou didst meet thy death!'
The skull remained completely silent.
Tenali asked again: 'Speak, skull!'
Not a whisper emerged.

The King grew furious:
'Tenali, thou hast lied to thy King!
Guards! Take Tenali to the palace gate and strike his back with twenty strokes of the cane for insolence!'

As the guards seized Tenali, Tenali looked back at the silent skull, smiled through his pain, and addressed the King:
'Maharaj! Look at the skull now!
Did it not tell the absolute truth?
Yesterday, it warned: "Loose speech brings a man to grief!"
Because my own tongue spoke too loosely yesterday about talking skulls, I am receiving twenty strokes of the cane today!
The skull did not need to speak with vocal cords; its lesson was delivered upon my own back!'

King Krishnadevaraya stopped in his tracks, realizing the profound, self-sacrificing wit of Tenali’s demonstration.
The King ordered the guards to release Tenali immediately, rewarded him with twenty gold coins instead of cane strokes, and had the lesson inscribed upon the gates:
'Guard thy tongue, for an unruly tongue digs an early grave.'
moral: Loose talk and unguarded tongues bring swift ruin; silence is the fortress of the wise. [KN]
